questions.hint: A slip system needs two pieces of information: an allowed plane and a direction lying inside it.
questions.explanation: Plastic slip moves dislocations along a direction in a slip plane. Dense atomic rows and densely packed planes often favor easy slip. FCC has four distinct {111} slip-plane orientations, each with three in-plane <110> directions, so 4 × 3 = 12 slip systems. The three-direction count is per slip plane, not the entire cubic direction family. BCC has dense slip rows but no truly close-packed plane.

questions.hint: Separate the machine measurements from the geometry-normalized material quantities.
questions.explanation: A load cell measures force and an extensometer measures gauge-length extension. Engineering stress is σ = F/A₀ and engineering strain is ε = ΔL/L₀. questions.hint: Balance the thermodynamic drive to form new material against how quickly atoms can diffuse.
questions.explanation: A time-temperature-transformation diagram uses temperature vertically and time, commonly logarithmic, horizontally. questions.hint: Ask whether carriers are already available or must first gain energy to reach accessible states.
questions.explanation: Metals have accessible nearby electronic states; semiconductors have a small gap and insulators usually a larger gap. Thermal excitation in a semiconductor creates conduction electrons and valence-band holes. In metals, thermal vibrations, impurities and deformation defects scatter carriers and usually reduce conductivity. In intrinsic semiconductors, heating creates more carriers and generally raises conductivity despite mobility changes.
questions.misconception: Do not apply the metallic temperature trend blindly to intrinsic semiconductors. Carrier concentration and carrier mobility are separate factors.
optionReasons: Conduction electrons and holes play different majority/minority roles in n-type and p-type material. For this question, that alternative does not satisfy the required relationship. Do not apply the metallic temperature trend blindly to intrinsic semiconductors. Carrier concentration and carrier mobility are separate factors.

questions.hint: Separate a specimen’s length and area from the material’s intrinsic electrical response.
questions.explanation: For a uniform conductor, R = ρL/A, so ρ = RA/L. Resistance depends on geometry; resistivity at a specified state is a material property. Conductivity σ = 1/ρ has units S/m. Charge neutrality does not require equal mobile carrier populations in a doped material.

Band-gap energies are in eV; shallow impurity levels are typically in meV, a thousandth of an eV.

questions.explanation: Silicate glass is an amorphous network based on silicon-oxygen units. Modifying oxides alter connectivity and properties. These comparisons are relative to composition and use.

questions.explanation: In the chapter’s ideal hard-sphere model, radius-ratio intervals correspond to coordination 2 (<0.155), 3 (0.155–0.225), 4 (0.225–0.414), 6 (0.414–0.732) and 8 (0.732–1). The shapes are linear, triangular, tetrahedral, octahedral and cubic. For NaCl, 0.102 nm / 0.181 nm ≈ 0.564, so the model favors 6-fold octahedral coordination. For FeO, 0.077/0.140 = 0.55 gives the same interval. Ratios are dimensionless; these rules are approximations.
